entries.note: “Highly doubtful” expresses probability rather than a firm prediction.
Whether Amodei supplied evidence is checkable separately. The combined claim also asserts his private purpose in making the prediction.

entries.test: Public demonstrations and documented deployments of Anthropic software available by June 16, 2025 would show whether it could replace workers in their jobs.
entries.note: The profanity reinforces a categorical product-capability claim.

entries.test: Research available by June 16, 2025 would establish whether there was substantial evidence of widespread AI job displacement.
entries.note: The concession about some jobs is not an antecedent condition.

entries.test: Employment research and documented deployment outcomes available by publication would show whether capability limitations were the main reason LLMs were not replacing workers widely.
entries.note: The later explicit statement about displacement at scale supports this reading.

entries.test: Documented AI replacement failures and subsequent hiring records would show whether companies hired back the workers they had dismissed because of AI hype.
entries.note: Rehiring depends on the stated failure event, which he also calls inevitable.
He asserts the purpose of the scare tactics, rather than demonstrating their effects on valuations or fundraising.

entries.test: Public reporting and research available by publication would show whether companies had demonstrably replaced entry-level employees with AI.
entries.note: “This” follows several concerns, including premature adoption and reduced training investment. The normalization selects one referent more confidently than the passage warrants.

entries.test: Workplace studies and demonstrated AI deployments available by publication would show how much of ordinary jobs AI could actually automate.
entries.note: This is a broad but empirically assessable capability claim.

entries.test: Public audience analytics, coverage patterns, and research on responses to job-loss headlines would test whether clicks and fear drove the narrative's spread.
entries.note: “Not because of evidence” adds an exclusive causal contrast absent from the quoted sentence.

entries.test: News archives through June 16, 2025 would show whether any reports documented companies replacing employees, rather than freelancers, with generative AI.
entries.note: “I can find no stories” is weaker than asserting that no documented stories exist.

entries.test: Employment studies and documented business deployments through publication would show whether generative AI was replacing workers widely.
entries.note: “At scale” has a plain reading of widespread displacement in this context.

entries.test: Public capability evaluations and workplace deployment studies would test whether gaps between advertised and actual capabilities explain limited worker replacement.
entries.note: The relevant advertised capabilities concern replacing workers.

entries.test: Demonstrated deployments and professional evaluations of systems available at publication would show whether AI could perform accountants', doctors', or competent writers' full jobs.
entries.note: The questions are immediately answered, making these assertions rather than unanswered rhetorical questions.

entries.test: Independent evaluations of then-current deep research products would show whether they reliably delivered accurate, sourced research for their advertised tasks.
entries.note: The surrounding discussion supplies a practical product-performance reading.
“Carrying real legal risk” strengthens “can cause genuine legal risk.” The speed improvement is separately checkable, but the extracted combination includes a possibility claim.

entries.test: Public studies and documented engineering experience would show whether LLM tools provided benefits while leaving substantial software engineering tasks or problems unresolved.
entries.note: “Far from a panacea” qualifies a concrete claim of limited utility.
The mental-health causal claim is separately testable. The combined proposition also claims nobody thought about the consequences before launch.
“This” refers to the uses just discussed; the normalization expands it to every current use case. “Transformative” expresses his assessment of their significance.
“Generic” and “truly life-changing” supply no shared standard of significance here.

entries.test: Public engineering studies and documented workflows would show whether LLMs provided practical benefits in software engineering by publication.
entries.note: The following examples make “value” a claim about practical utility.

entries.test: Public developer surveys, workflow studies, and production practices would show whether some engineers gained substantial speed while withholding trust from LLM output for production.
entries.note: The claim concerns some engineers, not every engineer using LLMs.
The proposition attributes an inflationary purpose to the terminology. Advertised capabilities could be checked separately against actual performance.

entries.test: Public analyses of software engineering duties and LLM performance would show whether responsibilities beyond writing code prevented straightforward replacement of engineers.
entries.note: The proposition explicitly explains the claimed replacement limitation.
“Might” states a possibility without a firm predicted outcome.

entries.test: Public employment research and documented company cases available by publication would show whether entry-level engineering jobs had been lost to AI rather than outsourcing or other causes.
entries.note: This concerns the evidence available when the post was published.

entries.test: A public corpus of contemporary AI coverage would show how media outlets used “powerful” and whether they applied “agent” to ordinary LLM activity without autonomous action.
entries.note: “Uncritically” replaces the stronger assertion that the media does not understand the technology.
The claim attributes a deliberate marketing intention, rather than merely an observable effect of the terminology.
“Doesn't really seem to be doing much” supplies no shared domain or standard for measuring activity or impact.
“Anyone” adds a universal claim about users. The passage does not identify which bubble problems or what would make them obvious.
“Does not say much” becomes “show only,” and the normalization adds an explicit conclusion about his analysis. No particular analytical claim is specified for testing.
The surrounding discussion makes the acquisition valuation the referent of “unlikely.”

entries.test: Public usability studies, product changes, and task-completion comparisons over time would show whether everyday products deteriorated and added generative AI features that obstructed users' tasks.
entries.note: The extracted proposition omits the separate allegation of intentional degradation for profit.

entries.test: Public publisher traffic data and studies comparing search referrals with and without Google AI summaries would show whether those summaries caused substantial traffic losses by publication.
entries.note: “Taking traffic away” attributes the losses to Google's summaries.
